Hey Guardians!


Missed the first update? Click here! Now, onto our new news!  


We’ve crunched the numbers, ran many playtests, and crunched some more numbers, but the community mission is just about ready to reach your main screens in our next update. 


We recently unveiled at PAX West our latest gameplay mode—One Shot Mode—and our community mission will be part of that update later this year! 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/0b8d9744b6c220a58387aae4113ee74bf1e00b3f.png"]We’re in our new game mode era


Now, onto the nitty gritty details… 

Revenants? Added

Teleporters? Added

Mimics? Double added!

Length? So long you guys

Difficulty? Ehehehehe… 

There were a lot of elements you all voted for, so once you put them all together, you get this! 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/41c30545f244a3fe8d609c53d178c1614db4fce8.png"]Just kidding! Can you imagine?
  

While this won’t be the FINAL look of the mission, rest assured, this has everything that our community voted for, and possibly even more! 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/68d4e332821f65f306737f58fe9dd22950746091.png"]This will all make sense once you play.  


Ok THIS is what you’ll be greeted with once you download the new update later this fall:  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/fe67e2b5ce64adb92d20d27fab4f6d07d3f2062d.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/458d705b64ac7bbccda70aa3c2a94fe4e4203fcf.png"]It’s so CLEAN


Thank you to Discord user CaramelKhorne (amazing username btw) for the name suggestion! We simply couldn’t pick any other name than this one. 


Our next update will be… gameplay! Stay tuned for more info in the following weeks, including more looks into our upcoming Patch 1.5!


Stay connected with us through our socials and through our official Discord server for more announcements on upcoming events and updates. 


Have a great day!

The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Sunderfolk Animation Style Guide
notes.content:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/a37fa3c9d5f66ba5ac4b0c912978087c64738b1c.png"]

**Gremlin editor's note: This guide features prototype character models. Enjoy the blast from the past AND the learning!


SUNDERFOLK ANIMATION STYLE GUIDE
Author: Alvin Geno
Updated 12/12/2022


What is the Sunderfolk Animation Style?
Our animation style is best described as designed reality. Design is used to describe the hand crafted choices to clarify the timing, posing and intent of the choices being made while animating.

What is unique about our game?[olist]
We need the poses to clearly show what our character's role is in the game. The character’s overall body language, type of weapon and combat  proficiency (How skilled they are), should be immediately readable from the game camera.

Our game is turn based  so we must always think about where the player's eye is looking. Use anticipations as a great way to draw the players eye to what's about to happen.

Our main game camera is fairly far from the characters. We should make sure that our pose changes are large and clear enough to read from far.

Our characters are fairly detailed so we should always design a focal point. Think of where you want the audience to look the most. Think about a primary, secondary and tertiary read. Always make sure the player does not miss the most important  part of the animation.

Our game does not rely on quick player control and response. We always know what player state our animation will be transitioning to and from. This means we can author transitions straight into our animation clips where necessary for Polish.

Our game has many characters. As more characters get animated, always compare new animation content to existing characters to make sure we are not repeating choices.

Although our characters should be specific. We should leave enough room for the player to  add their own creative input as to what/who/why our character is the way they are.
[/olist]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/4730228cdbe283e88781a4b5ad4015fbbdd1412f.gif"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/fa4132b17068fc11a2b8a140c2a96cab237b179b.gif"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/1130c2d373cbc7e70a3288a452cbb0906c30196c.gif"]
Sunderfolk Animation Principles:[olist]
Character Specificity
[olist]
The character brief will always be your starting point. Always think about how this character would do the specific action. If the choice you make can be put on another character and it still works, you have made the wrong choice.

Below is an example of a character brief:


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/f34c0fbf61812a582ca4bfdcca462285fd1681c1.png"]
[/olist]
Strong shape design
[olist]
We need to pay extra attention to the overall character posing and the shapes being created. This helps make sure we clearly understand what we are looking at from the game camera
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/b74612adb162162a62d614b29e5deab97ea6ea68.png"]1. Clear line of action. This should inform us where the character is coming from and where the character is going.
2. Clear directionality of weapon. We need to define a clear sense of where the character is looking and what they intend to do.

Make sure to define a very Clear silhouette from all game camera angles.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/23d98f5bdda2c08834d32dbe47702ab2fd58478c.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/db61c8cc312bbda581125ca711a2a2b970efc7b9.png"]

When designing a pose make sure to break up angles of the body so they do not perfectly align with any axis.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/37e1e5096674c1258f711cf0555be529ad1f412a.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/1be4bfd2dbe9f6ec0d5a7bbccd71ea87ba04ed8f.png"]

We must be intentional with character balance. The character weight should feel intentionally distributed. This means they are balanced when they are supposed to be balanced and off balance when intentionally designed to show direction of movement. See Green Lines below
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/4c4491f7c0da5edfb3f95843d3dadabd6ebd46dc.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/50a9df86f21203670b3edaf66ebb2b9ae53abdcb.png"]

We need to Incorporate tilting, Overall rhythm and twist throughout our pose design to keep it dynamic.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/c12d57562eda52f60d06fcd6b31b83587c79a8fa.png"]

Each character should be easily associated with a general overall shape. Try and keep this in mind as you define the different poses.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/53bd552b196bb4e22e293931e8b756210b99bf20.png"]Big Hero 6 (2014) Image property of Disney

We should also think very carefully about the transitional poses between our main core poses. What is commonly referred to as breakdowns or inbetweens. Wherever possible think of simplifying into basic geometric shapes.
[olist]
Example from God Of War (2018) Property of Sony Santa Monica Studios.  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/e048370d32c4c502c40e3b2a709576808347519c.gif"]Nice simple and clear overall shapes that communicate direction. They also communicate an overall sense of force through the squashing and stretching of the overall shape.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/bc124a0822fc505dce752b23e87ecb03c0d06035.gif"]Strong and clear poses make it easy to understand the action despite the character having an overall complex silhouette.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/02006525fc22d2d5ed2149e4fb8f5b20d35e4b9f.gif"]
[/olist][/olist]
Appeal
[olist]
Appeal is referring to making choices that when combined make our animation desirable to experience. 
Ask yourself  the following
[olist]
Do users want to look at this?

Does this feel satisfying and impactful?
[/olist]
Appeal should be considered both at a single pose basis, and also across frames during the animation. The overall performance should bring delight.
Example:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/5008252d075ef3925d891ac77abf8e36a224a7fd.jpg"]Norman Rockwell’s Proud Professor (1940)
[olist]
Norman Rockwell often made many intentional choices to allow his art to bring the most delight to his audience.
[/olist][/olist]
Clarified timing
[olist]
In our Game the timing should be caricatured to support the intent of the character. Make things faster to clarify expertise. Make things slower to suggest stability and/or carefulness. 
Remember, the timing will be specific to each character. 
Some characters are heavy so always ask yourself: How can we use timing to emphasize how heavy they are?

Contrast:
Make sure to place moments of stillness close to moments of fast motion to better contrast and exaggerate each other. 
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/9ba8fca1a9d94a989ab040d63d654ee6bf77f6de.gif"]

Texture:
Make sure to vary the rhythm and cadence of the animation phrases to keep the animation  interesting.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/795292f34670593c5e0879dca0ba707a83993923.gif"]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/95309c3689dacd92acff71c217645f3f0d3dab90.gif"]A phrase is a clear movement that supports a single smaller idea within a bigger movement sequence. E.g
[olist]
For the Bigger Movement Sequence of Firing an Arrow, the phrases would be:
[olist]
The Anticipation of pulling the bow string

The Action of Releasing the string and Firing the Arrow

The Settle back into the Ready/Idle pose.

[/olist][/olist][/olist]
Physical believability
[olist]
Physical believability is not to be confused with Realism. We should reference reality to inform our choices but caricature and design our animation to deliver the feeling we want the user to take away. 
[olist]
Take an example. In the Attack_SingleArrow animation for the Ranger. We do not animate the Ranger removing the arrow from the quill on the Rangers back in a physically correct manner. 
In fact, We add just enough poses to communicate that the Ranger is reloading but focus on the smoothness of the timing. The goal here is to allow the Ranger to look comfortable and efficient with this motion. Emphasizing the fact that the Ranger has done this countless amount of times.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/20c5a94bd71a9261cbeac1827697f35e36fe6627.gif"]In full speed it is physically believable
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/4730228cdbe283e88781a4b5ad4015fbbdd1412f.gif"]

Also note. In the example above the Ranger shifts weight forward onto the ranger's left foot before being able to lift up the Ranger’s rear foot. This motion is rooted in real physics. Please refer to real life for inspiration when animating our characters.
[/olist][/olist]
Fluidity and Readability
[olist]
Fluidity is all about how our poses change from one frame to another. We should always consider the following  
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/41e58d4537acfcae4ca5d258b204125070bcf45e.gif"]


FLUID EXAMPLE
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/02006525fc22d2d5ed2149e4fb8f5b20d35e4b9f.gif"]
[olist]
Does the next pose clearly flow out of the previous pose?

Does the pose clearly communicate what the character is doing?

Is this the Hero pose? If so, what can I do to make sure the audience sees this hero pose clearly?

How is the overall shape of each of the main body parts flowing from one frame to another? Is the spacing too much?

What are my focal points and how do I contrast them from other movements to direct the eye of the viewer?
Please note how the draw-overs on the FLUID EXAMPLE on the right really exaggerate the amount of squash and stretch. This helps with readability from the game camera

[/olist]
Fluidity is also expressed in how the various animation clips flow into each other. 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/31729bbf1c0217728e17ad96ae17a8b18bd5cd46.gif"]

Metroid Dread (2021) Property of Nintendo Entertainment

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/660c4773fb8de29097f83fef8567f6d30f8dd83a.gif"]So we should take extra care to make sure to maintain momentum across animation clips. E.g.
[olist]
Idle → Walk

Walk → Ready

Attack → Ready

… and more
[/olist]
Designed Transitional Shapes are very important. Wherever possible think of designed shapes that flow in and out of each other.  Always preserve the overall volume of the character.  Think about squash and stretch as an animation principle. Exaggerate the squash and stretch to be readable from the game camera
[/olist]
Fun
[olist]
Have fun with the animation. Take all the previous principles. Mix, match and experiment within those expectations. Allow the character description to inspire you to surprise the audience with a unique animation choice. We have characters based on real world animals. Let their unique anatomy and movement inform your choices. [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/7017eb74b25251915d5f505348b4b0097228f41f.gif"]

Moss Book 2 (2022) Above Animation by Laura Ivy Lico. Property of PolyArc. Included for reference purposes only.

 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/102527cce549fea994b1a25b3473ea1b6fb058b6.gif"]

Reference from other animals can inspire fun ways to accomplish animation. Image above could be used to inspire a fun death animation. Courtesy of @viralhog on youtube. 

Remember to be inspired by other well timed and textured animation [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/52675d9b0a2f5b43cd4f9665055963c37f473596.gif"]

Video Courtesy of Pixar Animation Studios. Piper (2016)
[/olist][/olist]

Sunderfolk Animation Process:
Game Camera should be prioritized. In fact, We expect to review the animation from all views in the provided Game Camera Rig.
 1. Pose Exploration
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/89a00793a3c8a6500aa330663f3cb8a6903cd8a4.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/b543de9b3fbd17d9ed32f7f3a53bba2983686dcf.png"]Image courtesy of Alvin Geno. Warcraft Arclight Rumble (2022)



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/30591d70a8caf396436a07fdebf8066d8a3849f7.jpg"]Image courtesy of Steve Hendershot. Undisputed Street Fighter: A 30th Anniversary Retrospective


At the beginning of every new character exploration is pose exploration. It's the most important part of the process.


The goal here is to quickly iterate and experiment with poses to learn what works and what doesn’t work for our character.


The quick iteration allows us to quickly get feedback and see what this looks like.
Please note: This is also a good time to show video reference. However, the video reference will not be used as ground truth because we will only commit to ideas that have been illustrated on the character rig.

[olist]
Most important thing is the character brief. Refer to it often to inform the choices you make with the character.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/f34c0fbf61812a582ca4bfdcca462285fd1681c1.png"]Though there is no limit to what kind of poses an animator can explore. It’s important for the animator to experiment with poses that will inform the animation clips we intend to create.
In this case… Idles, Attacks, Walks, Fidgets, knockdowns…e.t.c.
[olist]
At this stage it is important to gather as much reference as possible to make your choices as specific as possible.
[/olist]
All the pose explorations should be in a single Maya file.
[/olist]
2. Animation Blockout
The goal here is to build upon the feedback from the pose exploration phase to clearly describe what the animation will look like in the most efficient way possible.


We expect a clear breakdown of the following


[olist]
Step 1: Core Poses
Core Poses are the images we want the player to remember the most from the animation clip. These should really capture the personality of the character. They should build upon the strong shape design principle.  


Examples: Ranger_Base_Attack_SingleArrow (4 poses) [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/1019df24de6a7c9ea0d9c894e9b4b94aed980dc9.gif"]Ranger_Base_DamageFront (4 poses) [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/736a68d46dc3845e1ff5784b3339641f2a720cc2.gif"]Ranger_Base_Attack_ArrowBarrage (4 poses) 
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/d6b70f32c615507403fda6d2e58f50ec33a08f75.gif"]
[p align="center"]
~End of Core Pose examples~

Step 2: Transition Poses
These clearly describe how we get in and out of the core poses. These poses will help describe the physical believability of the character.
Timing Should be clearly defined. We want to get as much of a sense of the intended impact as clearly as possible.

Examples:
Ranger_Base_Attack_SingleArrow(8 Poses)
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/9fa3f6c2d26ee0b724baf5a9f53c7ae23c69de42.gif"]Ranger_Base_DamageFront (8 Poses)
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/413ba8abb42e50c1a4c441dc1652e54ab8db0968.gif"]Ranger_Base_Attack_ArrowBarrage (7 Poses)
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/815e55ed8d2fe5ecce8c5aeb086262cec530a7cd.gif"]~End of Transition Pose examples~

**Special Exception**
Please note that for the Walk Cycle Blocking pass, the legs should have enough poses and/or be splined enough for us to test without foot sliding in engine. See example below [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/4ec651a3407c1f2ddca9a44ce7e317cad584e979.gif"]~End of **Special exception**~
[/olist]


At the end of the Animation Blockout stage. Submit the animation for review!!


3. Animation Refinement
At this stage there should be no surprises. All the ideas were locked down in the previous pass. This stage is making sure the animation is smooth and the intent from the Core Animation Blockout is not lost. After this pass the animation should be shippable.

Examples:

Ranger_Base_Attack_SingleArrow
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/4730228cdbe283e88781a4b5ad4015fbbdd1412f.gif"]Ranger_Base_ReadyLoop
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/8ca10dc83d074279baf05937462c6b6a5a240b0c.gif"]Ranger_Base_WalkLoop
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/1130c2d373cbc7e70a3288a452cbb0906c30196c.gif"]
4. Animation Polish[olist]
This is the last 10% of the animation to take it from good to great. This is not necessary upfront but afforded to us if we run the production schedule well.

The following should be done in this stage
[olist]
Animate all the extra accessories for the character

Track (and polish up) the arcs of all the major focal points of the body.
Areas to track for intentional arcs/lack of arcs:
[olist]
Hips

Chest

Base of neck

Head

Nose

Shoulders

Elbows

Wrists

Knees

Feet

Weapon extreme points. E.g. the end of an arrow, hammer, bow, e.t.c.
[/olist][/olist][/olist]
~END~

notes.title: Design-a-Mission Update #1 - Setting The Stage
notes.content:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/1917942b9a02517e5b7beb40b2fdb2508845f534.png"]

Hey Guardians!



You voted and our design team heard! The community collab mission has been underway for a few weeks now, and we’re pretty pleased with the progress. We’ll be updating everyone on the process for creating this event, starting… NOW! 



As a refresher, here’s the criteria that our amazing community voted for:  



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/f275720442b3d2931a138f73ba104c17a0a70e56.png"]
[p align="center"]THIS IS WHAT YOU ASKED FOR


Once we had the final votes for everything, we shipped them off to our design team, who immediately got to work! 



[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcdKcuZ0PATRGJIL50QW46TszecHMvy7LLC6iknbV_wF8-VkcnH2R5w5TK4u0jg-goeM18XkL3SQOJ_Uyo9RRjJa8-B-F9bCpd-bpXOz657w_PQrxfne6wCunAVrdTvSWOTNqT3dA?key=CCCWi4Xpikrpv-d0J5beXA"]

[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeVCsb2xqdrrhDnU7YQS7j0nzqfY2HeDHG8At56ypJenWzU7TVc7E7tcwtds4sbgW8aPqrnJtxX4zLmJcmgHCP1S2u5VCiPK50xyLl8Qjwpz00EGxlGClzACT9o2HljmlIX4Du8qA?key=CCCWi4Xpikrpv-d0J5beXA"]
[p align="center"]Game design


Then after that is picking the best map that matches the gameplay, and of course, what our community voted for!



[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfFz36XwAl7HBvuEmL9j-jVgSvovB8MaAt2z5FkJcrzso2qBBVeZQjoYWuFN10ipgPfFrzmxHzb4VAn4WlC8C__XPHgUA9S8zarGHavzUnGtdi19r0XCdr5sQi6Ygs_2BvNmrMqfQ?key=CCCWi4Xpikrpv-d0J5beXA"]
[p align="center"]One of theeeeese is the final winner! Can you guess which one it is? 



After some thinking, light touches of creativity, and design madness, the concept begins to form: 



[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdAx3VaIYQDT17F0gz0MorXUD2myUPJNP6UDmyFzmV78wXAOwD2Ff--c35vqMFkUysyGEYIBFk7uNG1lj_kg8K4bf-QG-lpuWQnqXD8rXeW0hOg4IabASXXGE8l7nGXHu51cIibGA?key=CCCWi4Xpikrpv-d0J5beXA"]
[p align="center"]Memes are vital to the design process. 


After some more brainstorming and iteration, a gameplay loop forms, and with that, a mission begins its first steps into the world. 


[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd9LW5LnllaW60NNOT0GABU2zchSUEo1GSLYW78HMPIbUENqLOq0umhDY4-0lELIEfq-xc0mj54oZwPfDozFp8rQwvb5kkLQdSsnF7dyu6QjS2xy4Cgy911MQunu2SdZIBfe5XouQ?key=CCCWi4Xpikrpv-d0J5beXA"]
[p align="center"]Button Mushroom decided to block the level reveal. The little rascal! 


Stay tuned for our next update where we’ll reveal the map and the mission name! That’s right, the community voted for the name too! You can see the results of that on our Discord! 


If you simply can’t wait for the community mission reveal and you happen to be attending PAX West this year, we HIGHLY recommend stopping by! You might just be able to have your wish fulfilled. <3



We’ll see you soon, Guardians! 

The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Sunderfolk Update #4 - 1.4.1 Hotfix Notes
notes.content:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/59c9beaf8903e53da323830dee189bb0686fe703.png"]

Hello Guardians! 



We’ve been hard at work on fixing disconnection issues that have been affecting some Sunderfolk players, and we’re excited to have a fix for our Guardians. 


Hotfix 1.4.1
Fixed an issue where some players would experience frequent disconnections between the Sunderfolk main screen and phone controller app. 

This particular issue was caused by some firewalls dropping a required server connection due to limited network activity over the connection. This disconnect would most likely have been experienced while playing remotely over the Internet. The game now handles this situation better.

Please note, this hotfix may not prevent every possible network disconnection issue, and we always appreciate your feedback and reports for finding and squashing bugs.



Thank you!

The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Sunderfolk Update #3 - 1.4 Patch Notes & Summary
notes.content:
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXewDjKumDYkqNBSSfuC1uI75GPls-KFOc9A_UESdJ4XawtYkMPqRUReoq9oCZVMxx-Kd69Y3ss9fuH6C0MVuNTc8URepaCybOlUGKpGposXPhiozDbMsuhj5078KQOVcc9HDiYtSg?key=dXOucwgLmqQ9mGthZxm1kLxP"]

We discovered that you can, in fact, make a salad too powerful. Image credit to Discord user SilentBob4207. 



Hey Guardians!

You’ve spoken, and we’ve heard! We’ve been collecting your feedback and seeing where Sunderfolk shines and where it needs polish.


This latest patch focuses on some popular community requests, as well as an expressive new feature.😁 


What’s New / Priority Fixes in Sunderfolk 
Now introducing: Emotes

Players can now use Sunderfolk emotes with customizable text during combat and in-town. 

[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeazcNiQ6OhmRBs7WFEmycE-Ud4Yeu99CGI-YgVNpgwAQR-Eh2rNnnkrISZ6D9HzdgdzPAP76nGdmNOY4QtBkTVDZ_H2L_hrwLfTqILBkFVmtbv6h-W0qSjM3wcApzrrERn_MvYbQ?key=dXOucwgLmqQ9mGthZxm1kLxP"] Just click the Smile icon and go nuts! This will appear in town and during missions! 

[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf5GPiX2JiHenkpt6U3IyK0UkWriAPWcF37zRZUBds1OkoTuwR_rtLyJ0iDoGTqh7B4zEBNgaPbDY1bY_Rz_PukHxWWDZ0OPW2PRWIpyhN32R8C0NAzKm-O11AB-phW5uEzQm1s?key=dXOucwgLmqQ9mGthZxm1kLxP"]

Renameable Player Prompts

Were you too much of a loremaster and now you have to show your campaign to your family? We’ve got your back! Players can now rename the in-game prompts through the Shared Settings menu. 

[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfvWy99FMDWhDXyxv61AUBHvdY0IArUgEhKDDO50qDovWchj98BWGW3SBj9wOPn5nxCFdDdUTM3NyuGH7fCW-jh4lYE_WAtg2qVvgMxQtvjL_462N-wuzkX4k3qLMRWZHqlxKA3eQ?key=dXOucwgLmqQ9mGthZxm1kLxP"]

Name/Rename Your Campaign

Players will now be able to name their campaign party as part of the Hero Select process, which will be used as the Save File name. 

Players may change their party name later via the Shared Settings menu.

notes.title: Beginner's Guide to Sunderfolk
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/36671f4e85e714db1e625630b7f99c84f01a0e85.png
Hey Guardians! Are you ready to jump into Sunderfolk?

No? Well good thing you stopped by here first!

Here you’ll find everything you need to know to get ready to leap into the Sunderlands and save Arden! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/25746a42fbd31c99f7f62bfb7a11cb490ddde7ea.jpg
YES, "LEAP" WAS LITERAL

Starting Your Campaign
Once you’ve chosen your friends to party with you (or are undertaking this adventure solo) you’ll start up Sunderfolk, and create a new campaign by scanning the QR code shown with your Sunderfolk Controller App! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/e2fb24f851d6135ff8ade7826eb5e67236ff5f7e.png

Tip: Playing remotely with friends and need some help? Check out our handy Remote Guide for those Sunder-friends who are physically apart! 

Once everyone has connected to the game by scanning their phone or tablet with the Controller App, then you’re ready to watch the intro cutscene and begin your Sunderfolk journey! 

Choose Your Character 
The playable characters of Sunderfolk have many titles, but they all share the same mission—to protect the townsfolk of Arden. There are six different characters to choose from, all with their own unique playstyle that fills a vital role within a party. 


 The Arcanist - Master the intricacies of the arcane!
 The Bard - Inspire and deceive with MUSIC!
 The Berserker - Channel your Rage and demolish foes!
 The Pyromancer - Engulf everything in red-hot flames!
 The Ranger - Hunt your opponent from a distance!
 The Rogue - Devastate prey with devious attacks!

Tip: Need a thorough guide on all of the heroes before making your decision? Don’t worry, we’ve got you covered! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/57973e55117b3cfb8e877be4d6c29a72034202ff.png
Dibs on the Pyromancer!

Combat in Sunderfolk
Sunderfolk utilizes party turn-based, strategy combat separated into Rounds. Each Round of combat encompasses:

 Character Turn - You and your party members take their turns
 Monster Turn - Your foes take their actions 
 Ally Turn - If you have NPC allies, they’ll act here

There are no turn orders for your and your party, allowing for flexibility in your strategies! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/db8c3b7165c5a29db0ac4ded319ffe9d2f0317b1.jpg
Though we do recommend making sure the Berserker takes all the damage. 

We’ve Put a Hex On You(r grid)

As you may have noticed above, Sunderfolk utilizes a hexagonal grid for the battlefield! This opens up a lot of possibilities, namely for the term “adjacent”! You’ll see that a lot in your character Skill Cards! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/07b474f5fc9215a048c5dc82414e885493a192d1.jpg
Drop YOUR favorite grid-shape system in the comments below!

An enemy (or ally) can be adjacent to you as long as the hex tile that they are on is touching your hex tile! 

These tiles can also have environmental hazards (sometimes caused by party members), and some are baked into the map itself! 

Tip: When you move, each hex tile counts as one movement! Pushing an enemy or swapping with an ally also counts as one movement. 

Mission Guide
Once you’re in a Mission, you can view your character Skill Cards, passives, equipped items, and remaining Fate Cards all in one place! The guide will also show enemy abilities, their own Skill Cards, and any environmental hazards such as Lava and Slime! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/f77272c04820584367cd494b9108b03cc620bf3d.png
Who needs memorizing rules and passives when it’s all in front of you? 

Town and Upgrades
The town of Arden is where our heroes reside, and your main focus is to defend it from forces that seek to destroy it. However, within its walls await colorful residents who are happy to provide services and conversation! Think of it as your refuge in-between combat missions. 

Once in town, you’ll be able to: 

 Befriend and deepen relationships with the townsfolk. 
 Rebuild and upgrade Buildings. 
 Craft and purchase equipment.

Each building you rebuild and upgrade will offer a new bonus for your adventuring needs! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/6a2331b0a94508fce44682c21cade38863a0f9d5.png
Equipment 
Equipment in Sunderfolk is focused between 3 core types:

Trinkets

 Trinkets offer extra boosts for combat. They range from dealing damage to nearby foes, buffing, or even healing you. 
 You can earn Trinkets by looting them after they’re dropped by defeated enemies, crafted in the Workshop, or purchased in the Market. 
 The Workshop must be built in order to craft and upgrade Trinkets. 

Meals

 Meals offer extra buffs for combat missions, such as gaining 1 Shield buff if you end your turn next to an ally. 
 You can purchase Meals at Sinclair’s Tavern once it’s rebuilt. 
 The menu will change each time a Mission is completed, so don’t expect the same one each time. 

Weapons

 Weapons are powerful tools that you receive once you’ve leveled up and rebuilt the Smithy. 
 Weapons can only be activated after completing their “Energize” requirement. These can range from dealing a certain amount of damage or having an ally take damage near you. 
 Weapons can offer different options for your build, such as giving you an extra movement if you complete their Energize requirement. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/3ea9e398700937acde9b5b27672fb84fbd8401cf.png

Once you’re equipped with your gear, you can take on any challenge in the Sunderlands! 

Now you’re geared, equipped, and ready for an adventure! Have more questions? Ask away in the comments below!

The Sunderfolk Team

 The Negative Fate Card “-2 Damage, Blind Each Monster in Range 2” now correctly inflicts Blind instead of Provoked.
 
Berserker “Grisly Force” Skill Card Adjustment

 The Berserker’s “Grisly Force” ability now ignores any active Shield buff on the Berserker to deal the intended damage when the “Deal” action occurs. 

Rogue “Penny Pinch” Skill Card Adjustment

 Fixed an issue where gold and loot did not always spawn on the map when a Rogue used their “Penny Pinch” Skill Card.

Rogue Chroma Fix

 Fixed an issue where the Rogue’s applied Chroma color reverted to default when gaining Evasion. 

General Bugs & Issues Fixes
Missions

 The Ogre Queen no longer uses “Retaliation” when under the “Confused” debuff. 
 Enemies will now automatically lose the “Provoked” status at the end of their turn. 
 Fixed an issue where Bosses no longer clear the “Root” debuff automatically at the end of their turn. 
 Fixed an issue where enemies with Teleport and Leap abilities were gaining Haste buffs with the “Frenzy” passive. 
 Fixed an issue where Guard Bug Allies summoned from Trinkets no longer skip their remaining actions when swapping with a Hero. 
 Ally attacks will no longer trigger enemies’ Frenzy passive in Challenging or Shadowstone difficulty. 
 Chirp is now able to use their Move action after activating her “Bulldoze” ability and dealing damage to enemies. 
 [This is a story-spoiler: Read at your own risk] [spoiler]Fixed an issue where a Round Timer is missing in (“All That Glitters”), causing the missions to be blocked from progressing. [/spoiler]

Character

 [This is a story-spoiler: Read at your own risk] [spoiler]Fixed an issue where Heroes would lose more than the intended one Skill Card when deselecting a Skill Card while under the effects of “Fear”.[/spoiler]

General Bug Fixes

 Fixed an issue where players may experience a main screen freeze after changing settings during missions. 
 Fixed an issue where spamming the “+” add button on Character Select causes a softlock for players. 
 Fixed an issue that was causing looping conversations.
 Fixed missing and broken audio events in-game. 
 Adjusted the description for the “Black Inkwell” trinket to match its functionality. 
 [This is a story-spoiler: Read at your own risk] [spoiler]The mission (“Sundered Shadows”) will be reset to start from the beginning if it was saved and players quit in-progress.* [/spoiler]

*Developer Note: Some patches for Sunderfolk may reset the specific mission you are on at the time of the update, if we’ve made changes to how that specific mission works. This will send you back to town, but it will improve your overall experience with the mission. We’ll aim to give more advanced notice if these resets are coming in future patches. Thanks for rolling with it! 🎲

Don’t see an issue you reported? Don’t worry, this is just the beginning of our upcoming patches, so stay tuned!

Thanks for playing Sunderfolk!

notes.title: SunderBlog: Guide to Remote Play
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/0a433bd9d87d24c70b75f0afc8292ae5cae63d02.png

Entering The Sunderlands… Together

While Sunderfolk has been crafted as a couch co-op experience, we all have friends that live in different parts of the world, and we’re looking to close that gap… digitally, at least. 

If you have a group ready to go but are unable to traverse time and space to play together, never fear! Playing Sunderfolk is only a few steps away! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/20b86ffc3c3c900b899ae3f574697839ecab443a.jpg
This could be us but you’re playing… from very far away. 

Steam Remote Play

To Host Sunderfolk with up to 3 friends via Steam Remote Play: 

[olist]
 Add your party members as Steam friends (if you don’t have them already) through the Steam client or through here!
 Launch Sunderfolk through Steam
 Shift-tab to bring up the Steam overlay

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/6e9118b7d56704fcdb46a7afec06be30937fbf0c.png

 Open your friends list and right-click on your party member’s name

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/899dc151cbeb62946a51fe6a79f8e3cc73fffb44.png

 Select “Remote Play Together”, then invite them to your game
 Your players will be able to join after accepting the invite on Steam!
[/olist]
Now, all your friends can watch your stream while playing along from their phones. The best part is, they don't need to own the game or even download it to play cooperatively! All they’ll need to do is download the app on iOS or Android and accept your invite, and scan the QR code to join the party!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/110857c53a0c76c191739da4c9a7b8aab6db7cfe.jpg

Playing on Discord

If you want to spam all of your Discord Nitro emojis while playing, you can also play Sunderfolk remotely with friends through Discord!

To stream Sunderfolk on Discord:
[olist]
 Start up “Sunderfolk” on Steam 
 Create / Join a Voice Channel (or a private DM call)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/a207272ca52c1bf7de57bb38785ab1d50994f573.png

 When in the voice channel, select “Screen Share” from the options on the bottom-left

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/c21c9416de3eb16fb701794450f02ad664f1195a.png

 On the “Applications” tab, select “Sunderfolk”. Make sure application noises are toggled on so your players can hear the in-game sounds. 
 Hit “Go Live” and stream the game to your friends!
[/olist]
Hot Tip: If you join our Discord server, you’ll be able to join a “looking for group” channel to meet new friends and form a  new adventuring party! 

We’ll see you in the Sunderlands on April 23, 2025! 

The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Sunderfolk - From Closed Beta to Launch
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/b66f4bcba3d0d6b4e4d6058ed0b7acf4554f7671.png

Hey Guardians!

Our Closed Beta officially ended on February 4th, 2025, after a month and a half of testing! 

During that time, we’ve received over 1200 feedback submissions, and had 1700+ members join us in our closed beta Discord server! 

Now, we’ve used that information to make Sunderfolk even better and ready for release! Check out some of the upcoming changes in store for launch day, and join us in counting down the big day!

Some Implemented Changes: 

Pacing

Many small changes that add up to a major impact on the speed of play. These changes help to streamline the pacing of gameplay: 

 Pulsing animation on the tile of Heroes that haven’t played yet this turn. Hurry up and take your turn!
 Movement and attack animations speed up when multiple monsters of the same type take their turns sequentially. This resets when a new monster type takes its turn.
 Increased the move and attack animation speed of most characters.
 Improvements to missions and Monsters to increase pacing:

[olist]
 Tower Defense: Stun Bug now only attacks 1 target, not 3.
 Minecart Mayhem: reduced number of webs.
 Lost in Swamp: re-arranged starting Oozes, increase NPC health.
 Oozes’ Fate Cards no longer spawn additional Oozlings.
 The Fungal Vale: changed Oozes to Redcaps.
 Shadowshard: moved barrels closer to teleporters.
[/olist]

Settings

Added more settings to allow you to remove UI and Narrative friction:

 Setting to let you Auto-Skip Narrative, Tutorials, and/or Cinematics.
 Setting to let you Auto-End your turn instead of needing to press the End Turn button.
 Added more configuration options for the “Hold to Skip” feature, allowing you to skip your actions without looking down at your phone.
 Added Exit to Hero Select to make it easier to add new Heroes to existing campaigns.


Difficulty

Improving the Difficulty curve to be more consistent across missions, while pushing to distinguish Brightstone and Challenging as more distinct difficulty modes. 

 Easier Brightstone Difficulty mode.
 Invincible NPCs.
 Harder Challenging Difficulty mode.
 All Monsters have Frenzy and become more powerful when they are:
 Attacked by a Hero.
 Unable to attack for the round.
 Stronger Monsters.
 More Elite Monsters Spawns.
 Shadowstone Difficulty Unlocked Automatically.


Heroes
After analyzing data and going through your feedback, we've made some balance changes to some Heroes!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/2a0658cae46cf42fae40dc6106b80944dd98ef49.png
Arcanist

 Arcanist is in a good spot; they've received balance tweaks to some spells.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/865387eb18e6de41fed96c59819224646a5d09d1.png
Bard

 Bard has some room for some extra power, so they received some damage and movement increases.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/ce2b503b03ec08635e8ba38d5709edfb3942ef49.png
Berserker

 Berserker's in a good spot; touching up some under-loved spells.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/ed20bb20e4c58e20970dd3bab51d7fa4bcb9556a.png
Pyromancer

 Pyro has a lot of power, so shifting some of that power around.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/94d3483028574135c386f69930658eb4bb51d238.png
Ranger

 Ranger has some room for some more power; they received some upgrades.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/f370040ccded15795edbf268fd90e11f8a2e6522.png
Rogue

 Rogue is in a good spot; made some changes to reduce player confusion.


Town

 Re-organized building upgrade rewards to more closely match the building theme.
 Added a new Market Shop that exchanges Favors for certain Trinkets to create an outlet for excess Favor items.
 Rewrote and added extra text to better describe certain building upgrade rewards.
 Level-Up celebration now happens soon as you arrive at Level-Up.
 Tavern Meals are now weighted, making it more likely newer unlocked / better meals are more likely to appear.


UI/UX

 Added a skip remainder of turn button in combat when taking your turn
 Implemented corner cutting on movement & targeting to help improve the ease of drawing your path
 Improved tablet UI support
 Better telegraphing for unique mission mechanics and rules (story spoilers below!):

[olist]
 Show which card is Feared in [spoiler] Shadow of Doubt mission. [/spoiler]
 Visual status effect for [spoiler] Ritual Healing Water Carrier and Fungal Friends Fungi alignment.[/spoiler]
[/olist]

Other 

 Improvements to disconnect handling and flow
 Removed the QR code which blocked too much of the screen when players disconnected
 More places where the game saves in Town
 Added in slide animations when stepping on Slime
 Lots of improved VFX, animation, and audio!


Just The Sunder-Start

Now, these are just some of the changes we’ve made for launch, and this is just the beginning! If you don’t see your feedback implemented here, we are planning post-launch patches that will include changes that we couldn’t add for our launch day. 

Thank you all again for your feedback, bug reports, and for joining us on this first step into Sunderfolk’s journey! We can’t wait to show you everything! 


 The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Sunder-Dev Diary #1 - The Inspiration Behind Sunderfolk
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/0a433bd9d87d24c70b75f0afc8292ae5cae63d02.png

Hi, I’m Erin Marek, Game Director on Sunderfolk. Since kicking off our closed beta back in December, we’ve been blown away by all the great feedback and questions in Discord.

These discussions inspired the team and me to share some insight into our approach to the game. Over the coming weeks, we’ll share some unique perspectives on our different disciplines, backgrounds, and how it all comes together to make Sunderfolk into a game we hope you, your friends, and your family will love. 

To kick off these developer diaries, I’d like to dive into the early development of the game and some of the things we hope to accomplish through Sunderfolk. 

Let’s rewind a bit to some of the earliest conversations around the game.

Kindling connection with familiarity 
When the team first started forming the initial concept of the game, one thing kept resurfacing again and again– how much we love the feeling of being together and playing tabletop board games with our friends and family. We set out to build something that inspired those same feelings through a video game experience.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/b0ac5eac0b3c6db04f93b6bcd731bf2599843f9f.jpg
Early concept art for Sunderfolk

At the time of those early brainstorms, Covid had made many of us feel isolated and alone, so there was a really strong desire to find a way to reconnect with those earlier days of just having fun together around the table or in couch co-op. The team started jamming on how we might create similar experiences through video games to make it a little easier for folks who aren’t as familiar with the genre. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/2f7654c681fe91b57b4c5c126d1b9d233fa4cc5e.jpg
Early pen & paper concept for Sunderfolk combat. See anything familiar?

Brightstone versus Shadowstone
With the goal of bringing folks together, it was super important for us to make the world around Sunderfolk approachable and inviting for a wide audience. We aimed to strike balance between creating a lighthearted, whimsical world while still allowing for moments of depth and seriousness. 

Our world is shaped by its underground setting, which heavily influenced the game’s themes and design. You’ll see plenty of bugs, mushrooms, stones, gems—elements that bring the environment to life. The overall story itself is another way we think about inviting players in, both novice and veteran. 

A lot of fantasy stories revolve around a classic good-versus-evil dynamic, which is something we really liked because it’s instantly familiar and easy to grasp. This backdrop naturally influenced our take on the good-versus-evil theme, leading us to the central conflict of Brightstone versus Shadowstone.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/3f55d8b8ff94bd0920e4e6c895effce07cb5a2a0.jpg
Early concept art for the town of Arden

What we’d really love for folks to take away after they play Sunderfolk is excitement to play more board games and D&D and tabletop games, especially new folks who maybe haven’t played those kinds of games before. 

For groups who have struggled to find the right game to play because it can be exhausting to set up a board game or for a GM to get content ready, we’re hoping that Sunderfolk can help reinvigorate their passion for revisiting those games.

I appreciate you all for taking the time to read this first developer diary! The next focus will be on how Sunderfolk was designed around collaboration and teamwork.


 Erin Marek, Game Director

notes.title: Meet Your Heroes: The Rogue
notes.content:
Mustelidae Miscreant 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/47debedb9af3fafdde78e7f5756525f214ab47a8.png

“If it isn’t my favorite"hero"! I bet you never thought you’d be called that. I know I didn’t!" - Sinclair, Tavern owner. 

The Rogue may look like they’ll stab you in the back for some loose change, and they may have at some point, but they are devoted to keeping Arden safe from other dangers. Their employer, Sinclair, trusts them implicitly with keeping the tavern safe, and knows all about their shady past. What that shady past is depends on you, whether it’s a previous smuggling job, previously from another city, or humbler origins in Arden.

Lord of Edges

The Rogue may primarily serve as a damage class, but don’t let that fool you—they can also be a reliable tank with their Shroud ability!

Shroud allows the Rogue to envelop themselves in shadow, allowing them to automatically dodge any damage source once, as well as deal extra damage when active. However, you’ll lose Shroud if you’re hit by any source of damage, so try to avoid that. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/bfa14812a83bd914a491c0409c92fbfa97b85a4a.jpg
It doesn’t go away with dealing damage though! Let your knives go brrrrr. 

Movement is key to a Rogue, as you can’t be adjacent to enemies in order for your Shroud to activate. Some abilities will remove Shroud automatically when you deal damage to grant buffs or debuffs, such as their Sneak Attack ability, which Stuns the enemy after attacking but removes your beloved shadow cloak. 

To help the Rogue get the upper-hand (and perhaps set up some backstabbing shenanigans) they receive the following Skill Cards after the tutorial section:


 Slice Twice: Move, hit an enemy twice, then move away or push them to get your Shroud ability. Best of all, Shroud gives you extra damage on that second hit! 
 Isolate: Get more movement to find the perfect prey, then deal damage. You deal extra damage if that enemy has no one adjacent to them! 
 Myriad Blades: Become an agent of the shadows by attacking, teleporting, and attacking again. Your enemies will never know what hit them. 


Balancing between being in the enemy’s face and moving away to activate Shroud is key to a Rogue, but there are always options to get right back in their face! Using the right Skill Cards can have you dancing between enemies and tanking for your friends without a care in the world. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/91cf28d179388beafed09f5e7c4c30362e149d63.jpg
Or, you know, to get loot. Priorities.

Once Rogues gain more experience, they’ll be able to add powerful Skill Cards into their arsenal, such as:
 

 Pennypinch: An ability for your sticky fingers! Move, then attack, which creates gold, attack, create more gold, then move!  
 Smoke and Mirrors: You thought the Arcanist made the only decoys? Attack, teleport away, and leave a decoy in your place. They’ll even attack the enemy after you move! 
 Soulthieve: Move, then target an adjacent creature with buffs. Steal those for yourself, then deal damage with your new buffs! The more you stole, the more damage you deal!


Of course, taking damage and dealing it back isn’t all the Rogue can do! With some key abilities, they’ll be able to heavily debuff enemies with Blind, Stun, and even Execute enemies! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/351ab7a78074ba64ab5bf15aee58a7ab37c51dc5.jpg
This is the most front-facing damage a Rogue has ever done. 

Shadowy Fate

As the Rogue grows, so do your Fate Card options! While a ton of Fate Cards will help buff the Rogue, there are just as many that focus on survivability and sneakiness! 

The Rogue can use Fate Cards to turn their builds into:

 Move and Stab: Give yourself extra Move to get Sneak attack back, or go for a new target mid-turn! 
 Decoy Diversion: Create Decoys in your place to confuse enemies or have them attack your foes! 
 Your Buffs Are My Buffs: Steal enemy buffs for yourself! They won’t need them anyways. 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/3618058d06222e28209498bfb8514842a914cd89.jpg
The pit dilemma: Do you push them off a cliff, or stab them to show them who’s boss? 

Ultimate Backstab

The Rogue’s Ultimate Ability, Thousand Cuts, lives up to its name and then some. 

This ability grants the Rogue a Teleport next to an unwilling victim, then deals damage! If they’re under 8 health after the damage is dealt, they’ll automatically be Executed. If they are defeated, you can repeat the entire Ability again. Wheeee! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/ac9ae0aa514f740c2d0b820ecb0597a870a10f68.jpg
He’s coming to GET YOU. 

And that’s a wrap on the Sunderfolk Heroes! 

Next on our agenda is a deeper focus into the combat systems of Sunderfolk, as well as some exciting talks straight from our developers. Stay tuned! 

-- The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Meet Your Heroes: The Ranger
notes.content:
Markhor Marker

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/72533002326ccb9b34f9be543fd1288360dc9def.png

It’s been great having ya living with me and the kid, and now everyone’ll see how great ya are too! - Batu, the town clothier. 

The Ranger is a new addition to the town of Arden, taken in by Batu. The Ranger now devotes themselves to protecting their new home with their powerful ranged abilities. When playing, your Ranger may be focused on hunting, recovering from a devastating loss, or a traveling soul. No matter what you choose as their background, the Ranger will always be the party’s supportive archer. 

Underground Strider
The Ranger is a perfect mix of damage and support, with focuses on ranged combat, debuffing enemies, and providing crowd control abilities. Their main source of damage comes from their passive, Precision, which lets you deal more damage when the range requirement is met and inflicts a debuff. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/2f68c797fdee7ccdaa789568bd81c5bdf84c3a76.jpg
Expose increases damage taken by +1, and that includes environmental damage! 

After completing the first series of missions, the Ranger will be able to use: 

 Hunter’s Shot - Fire an arrow straight at the enemy. As straightforward as their arrow. 
 Nock Back - Move, then push an enemy or ally back 3 hexes, then move again. Leaves Vines that can Root enemies or allow extra movement for allies. 
 Piercing Arrow - A line attack that lets the Ranger move into position, and fire up to 5 hexes away. 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/2e6e65cb7a114a3a3dbc4c185e8bce2d3ab09de2.jpg
Satisfying? Yes. Does it take a while to set up? Also yes. 

A Ranger is at their best when they’re away from enemies, but they can also buff themselves and leap away if they need to get in close. Their Spring Step skill allows you to attack, Slow their enemy, then Leap away to safety! If you land away from any monsters, you gain Haste and Strength! 

They also have light repositioning abilities that can not only be used to push away enemies, but can help you give your allies the needed push to get right into position and deal more damage! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/6794892555494f93eeceb9cd2aa767241fa84656.jpg
Give your allies a healthy push in the right direction. 

To add even more variety in their spells, the Ranger will also receive the following Skill Cards at higher levels: 

 Scout Ahead - Attack, Move, then debuff up to 2 enemies with Expose! Your Rogue and Pyromancer friends will thank you.
 Snaring Vines - Move, then create 3 Vines within 3 hexes of your location, then move again. Bait enemies into getting rooted, or help allies get to safety! 
 Wild Bloom - You don’t need rain for this super bloom! Unleash an area-of-effect attack, and create 2 Vines in any empty hexes within the affected area, then move! 


Piercing Fate

Similar to the other heroes, early-game Fate Cards provided for the Ranger focus on either self-buffs or debuffs, so you can choose to build your Ranger as more damage-focused or support-focused! 

Potential builds for mid to late-game Rangers can be:

 Debuff Hero: Anything and everything debuffs your foes. Draw an unlucky -2? Debuff. Grabbed a +1 but the enemy is still up? Debuffed for the next round. 
 Leap and Vine: Need to get away but want to leave a mark? Pick Fate Cards that grant you Leap but leave a Vine in the exited hex. Your enemies couldn’t pursue you if they tried. 
 Ranged is Good: Perfected the art of staying away from enemies? Use Fate Cards that buff your damage on top of your passive as long as you’re within the required range! Now that’s leaving your mark. 


Either way, keep your distance from enemies and you’ll be the hero of your party for the amount of versatility you bring to the table. 

Ultimate 360 No-Scope

Once they hit Level 6, the Ranger gets their ultimate Ability: Snipe.  

Snipe grants the Ranger 3 hexes of Move, then unleashes a powerful single-target attack that can be increased if the Ranger has any Strength buffs, and stacks with your passive ability. That’s one way to erase an enemy off the map. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/baa486be859539465a6912db7d24a6948011cf0a.png
Hit them so hard they report you for hacking. 

If ranged damage seems too safe and careful for you, then we can’t wait to introduce our next character! 

Up next is the Rogue spotlight! 

If you’d like to visit one of our earlier Hero spotlights, check out:

 The Arcanist
 The Bard
 The Berserker 
 The Pyromancer



Thank you!
The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Meet Your Heroes: The Pyromancer
notes.content:
Amphibian Conflagration  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/ccea89240e444910468429c9d0f19e4ba54c1df5.png

“Now you’re actually doing something you might do well; setting things on fire! But for Arden this time!” - Scorch 

While their sibling Scorch might not be the brightest ember in the furnace, they do know one thing: their little kin has a mighty fire burning within them. The Pyromancer has always had a reputation to strive for, and based on your preferences, their dreams may lie within being a leader of the people, finding purpose after a long slumber, or perhaps failed ambition will drive them. 

No matter how you choose their path, they will always be the warmth that their party relies on. 

Pyrotactics

The Pyromancer might look adorable, but they’re a confined inferno and they need to let it out.  Fire’s the name of the game, and unleashing it is the prize. The Pyromancer really gets their power by absorbing Fire and making it their own, then unleashing it through their skills. 

Each stack of Firepower, their passive ability, gives +2 to each attack, and they can stack it up to 3 times! This will also stack with any Strength buffs, so if you want to erase something off the map (with fire), the Pyromancer is for you. 

After completing the first few missions in Sunderfolk, the Pyromancer will be able to use: 

 Bouncing Blaze: Move, deal ranged damage, with a bonus of your fireball bouncing to an adjacent enemy. It’s a deadly hot potato! 
 Flame Breath: Move towards enemies and unleash a line fire attack that can hit up to 3 foes! 
 Meteor Crash: Become the fireball of your dreams. Leap 3, and deal damage to all enemies around your landing spot. You can also create your own Fire this way! 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/87f1d10ccad6929e05614861fd5ee489cac225bf.png
Fun Fact: The Pyro loves being surrounded by fire! Not fun for your teammates, though. 

The Pyromancer isn’t always just about raw damage! This is a game of strategy and tactics after all, and they’ll need to have a few extra tricks up their sleeve if they want to help their team out. Luckily, they do receive some great abilities that can help boost their survivability and overall tankiness. 

The Pyro can start to use the following Skill Cards at later levels: 

 Trailblaze: Become the fiery change you want to be in the world. Set 3 hexes on fire, leap to one of them, then deal damage to whoever is in range. 
 Cauterize: Did the Rogue take that last heal shrine? Move towards fire, choose an area with tons of it, then absorb it all and heal 2 health for each fire you absorb. Your teammates will appreciate the space back, too. 
 Friendly Fire: Make your friends nervous by targeting them after moving, then unleash some fire right on them and deal damage to adjacent enemies! Your friend won’t be hurt, physically at least. 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/3fc711eaecbb42ec20205f0d95e7c0b2ff06b30f.jpg
Look at that delighted face. No Rangers were harmed in the making of this screenshot. Well, not by the Pyro, anyway. 

Fiery Fate
What the Pyromancer makes up for in damage, they lose in mobility in early game missions.  However, you can eventually change that with the power of fate (cards)! 

You can either go the more damage route, or pick Skill Cards that can teleport you safety from danger. After all, enemies are going to want to hit the squishy salamander that made their friends go boom. 

Some Fate Card build options for the Pyro are:

 Leaping Away: Using Leap cards can be a massive help when you’re surrounded by enemies. With some built-in leap cards, you can truly become the frog salamander-hop master. 
 Absorb and Conquer: Using Fate Cards that allow you to absorb any adjacent Fire surrounding you is a great way to guarantee you’ll never run out of firepower. This also includes potential healing for any fire absorbed! 
 All the Fire: Why wait for Fire to appear when you can make it yourself. With each cast, you’ll be able to add more Fire to the board, which can set up some defenses as well as leave you with plenty of fire to absorb later. 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/e01eeb6d2640b5289ffe49682d89591c7fdf4642.jpg
Pair these Fate Cards with Meteor Strike, and you can leap frog your way across the map. If you’re lucky on the draw. 

Ultimate Fireball
The Pyromancer is no stranger to tons of damage, and their Ultimate ability, Inferno, truly embodies that sentiment. Inferno allows the Pyromancer to dominate the field by moving into position, and cast a massive area-of-effect fireball that damages enemies and leaves behind a roaring fire in each empty hex that the fireball hits. 

So if there ARE enemies left after that, they’ll be surrounded by, well, you know. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/3373d78dd1e842e7bd0547dde6ac807ff364a97e.png
A dexterity save won’t save you from this! 

While the Pyromancer is hard to top when it comes to dealing damage, they’re hardly a one-man show. If you want a good mix of support and long-range attacks, then we have the perfect character for you!

Stay tuned for the Ranger spotlight! 

If you’d like to visit one of our earlier Hero spotlights, check out:

 The Arcanist
 The Bard
 The Berserker 


Thank you! 

- The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Meet Your Heroes: The Berserker
notes.content:
Bear-rier from Pain 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/e658120d27b7d605b9acf0b1d8da83603137e186.png

“Benefits of growing up with you: Ogres don’t seem so scary.” - Bramble, the Berserker’s sibling. 

The Berserker has always been the reliable go-to animal for their younger sibling Bramble, and they continue that tradition by being a guardian of Arden. Your Berserker may have picked up a sweeter trade prior to their hero duties, be retired from their previous position as gate guard, or a travelling protector, but one thing is always clear—they always protect their fellow Sunderfolk. 

Load-Bearer

While the Berserker may seem no more than a simple tank at first glance, their wide array of combat abilities—paired with their staggering selection of self buffs—allows them to roar in the face of danger (sometimes literally!). 

Their passive is Protector’s Fury, which makes the Berserker take less damage and deal more damage as long it’s active. It’s not only effective against enemy attacks, but will also work for any external damage, such as environmental tiles like lava and fire. The only catch is that you need to be HIT first before it activates… so get in there and get mad! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/1260276a2cf515a0500bcb3c20c6f92c7e8c75a6.jpg
Are they ever really in danger, though? 

Once you clear the first set of missions, the Berserker has three main Skill Cards: 

 Bulwark: The tried and true tank ability. Move to position, then deal a nasty swing that provokes the enemy hit and gives the Berserker a shield. 
 Fling: Your best friend if there’s a pit involved. Move, grab an enemy (or a friend!) and [strike]yeet them aggressively [/strike]throw them where you think they should be. 
 Whirlwind: Surrounded by enemies? Good! Want to be surrounded by them? Move yourself and let loose your hammer to hit all enemies around you. 


The Berserker has little to no regard for personal boundaries and loves to get right up in the face of whoever might be in their way.. They’re an absolute unit of a Guardian, though, and that means reduced movement—which can sometimes hinder them from getting where they want (or need) to be. That’s why the Berserker also comes equipped with abilities that grant them lots of Move, like Bring It On, as well as ones that brings enemies to THEM.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/ea232d79513472225e06d48bf29b16c82d988d56.jpg
If you don’t shout “GET OVER HERE” while using Long Haul, you get -1 coolness. We don’t make the rules, we just let you know. 

The Berserker may seem less complex than some of our other playable characters, but that simplicity is only fur-deep. As they level up, the Berserker will unlock a wide range of abilities that make them one of the most fearsome creatures on the map, including: 


 Grisly Force: Move towards enemies, then deal 3 damage to yourself. Sounds grisly, but then ALL damage you’ve taken adds to the final damage you deal to the enemy. 
 Take Down: Thought the Berserker wasn’t scary enough before? Attack, then follow with a Move and another attack! Best of all, if you take down an enemy with the first attack, you’ll get a strength buff AND a shield! 
 Hibernate: Need to heal in a pinch? Move away from the scary things, shield yourself, then use your Rage to heal. You get extra health if you use this card with less than five health remaining. 


That’s just a taste of the Berserker’s rage, and they only get meaner as they grow stronger! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/da88249c668ef085256fb6048057e8ef1f5c76a9.jpg
Provoke ensures the enemy attacks you on their next turn. You made them mad! 

Provoking Fate

Like their fellow party members, the Berserker’s Fate Deck starts out simple, primarily focused on Strength and Shield buffs. However, as they level up, the amount of build options available to them through careful card selection growls grows! 

Fate Cards that grant Haste, Shield, or Strength are always good for early game Berserkers. For mid-game? Keep an eye out for cards that focus on crowd control so you don’t have to rely solely on abilities like Bulwark. 

As you progress, you’ll unlock Fate Cards with buffs like Retaliate! Or, you can stack your Fate Deck with nothing but Strength buffs, allowing you to transform your Berserker from a tanky bear into a… regular, scary bear. 

Some Fate Card builds for the Berserker can be: 

 Bear [strike]Totem [/strike]Tank: Become a true defense character. Stack Shields, Retaliate, and Heal cards so even your -2 Cards help you survive. 
 Charging Forth: Feel like your Berserker isn’t moving enough? Stack Charge buffs which let you move outside of your normal ability Moves and deal damage while moving. 
 Provoke, Throw, Repeat: Become a frustrating (for your enemies) combination of a taunting tank who makes enemies walk BACK to them for some more punishment. 


Ultimate Roar

Starting at Level 6, the Berserker gets their ultimate Ability: Roar! 

This ability gives them 3 hexes of Move, followed by a devastating area-of-effect damage blow coupled with a debuff to them, then finally shields each hero and ally nearby. It’s a war cry and massive attack in one fell blow! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/8adbf8fb4dad356d3c2883dd6eaca16ae1093114.png
You… made them mad. You really didn’t want to make them mad. 

However, if you want to leave damage to the professionals, might we suggest their fiery friend? 

More on the Pyromancer soon! 

If you missed one of our earlier Hero spotlights, check out:

 The Arcanist 
 The Bard


Thank you!

The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Meet Your Heroes: The Bard
notes.content:
Classical Chiroptera

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/184fb74da49ead5ab80c6f4672fa43511a89d7e1.png

“You played the most beautiful tune I’d ever heard! I knew then…that you were spending far too much time on recreation!” - Sentinel Treak 

Despite the best efforts of their adoptive guardian, Sentinel Treak (who’d much rather the Bard be a dedicated soldier, discipline above all!), the Bard devotes themselves to their craft and to protecting Arden. They were either exiled, a prodigal talent, or trained for other specialties, but how their ballad in Sunderfolk is crafted depends on you!

The Beat of Combat

Using the power of music, the Bard focuses on map manipulation as well as supportive buffs to make their team shine. Their passive, Two-Step, can really help a melee teammate close the distance, or allow for quick and easy buffs right before getting into attack mode. 

You can drop their Music Notes by swapping positions (as long as Two-Step is available), using certain abilities, or utilizing select trinkets and weapons to fill the battlefield with buffs. However, those can be trampled by enemies, so choose your positioning carefully!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/a876959cf94e76500e3294950a2f9a6c702dde8a.jpg
A trait so good, it becomes a powerful spell mid-game! Be the rockstar of your dreams. 

Once you’ve completed the tutorial missions, you’ll have the following Skill Cards in your repertoire: 


 Sharp Refrain: Move, deal single-target damage, then summon a Music Note next to the enemy you hit. 
 Siren Song: Move, enchant a friend or foe to walk towards you, then move yourself again! 
 Beat Drop: Leap right into the fray, push enemies away, then strut away in style. 


Controlling the map is truly their specialty, though, with abilities that can move either allies or enemies, depending on the situation! While their ability Siren Song is picked up right at the beginning of the game, being able to position allies or enemies for setups gives it longevity that’s truly unmatched.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/102b8a9257e6006890c3ba5f67910b4cb6fcc465.jpg
Damage, crowd control, AND drops buffs? What CAN’T music solve?

To complement their early board-blocking and bestie-boosting beats, the Bard will also receive the following abilities at higher levels: 


 Shield Sonata: Hit an enemy, shield whichever ally was next to that enemy, then walk towards friends and shield them again! 
 Power Chord: Deal damage to enemies around you, push them away, then buff your allies with some Strength! 
 Crowd Surf: The best movement and repositioning spell, use your Two-Step passive to great effect then deal damage based on how much you moved! 


Of course, you’ll get even more abilities as you level up and get stronger! And, with a clever selection of trinkets and/or weapons, you might even leave the Arcanist weeping in jealousy of your ability to manipulate your surroundings. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/65d0ecea30db32770e97225fad2c4374b1f5b430.jpg
Use your powers wisely! 

Playing With Fate

Just like all of our playable characters in Sunderfolk, The Bard’s Fate Deck will begin with the standard suite of cards that affect their attack damage output. 

As they level up, more nuanced Fate Cards will appear! Many of these cards will provide the Bard self-buffs, so that they can stay alive even if they've beat-dropped themselves into a sticky situation, while others may kick off a buff-et for your friends to feast on! 

The Bard can use Fate Cards to turn their builds into:


 ALL of the Music Notes:  Deal -2 to your roll? Get some Music Notes. Extra Move on a Neutral card?  You guessed it, Music Notes to accompany your small journey. 
 Vicious Enemy Mockery: Become the debuff champion and make enemies regret even targeting you. 
 Inspire and Revive: Want to Inspire your allies to attack enemies near them, without moving or using an ability card? Your Fate Decks can help! You can also set Fate Cards to Heal allies! All it takes is a lucky draw. 


Ultimate Performance

Their Ultimate Ability, Mosh Pit, is the grand finale to the Bard’s kit once they reach level 6. 
This ability gives the Bard five spaces of movement then deals area-of-effect damage to nearby enemies. But that’s not all! It also enchants all fellow party members, compelling them to move towards the Bard and attack any enemies within range after reaching their destination. It’s so punk rock.🤘! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/31917c6d2f986c3aa43113aa08cba49e719081be.png
The power of music compels you! 

No matter how good the Bard may be with positioning and support, they still can’t tank ALL of the damage…which leads to our next deep dive: the Berserker!

Stay tuned for more info on our beefy ursine guardian! 

- The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Meet Your Heroes: The Arcanist
notes.content:
Corvid Conjuries

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/4069e5996e0c878a844d381eee6312db43e89f08.png

“I’ll be the first to admit it; your magic is super bright!”  - Kazera

Much to the slight annoyance of their roommate, the oracle Kazera, the Arcanist has a powerful ability to manipulate magic around them. Your Arcanist can be reclusive, from a shady background, or be one to spot malicious intent from a mile away! 

Abilities, Mana, And You
This corvid conjurer focuses on casting abilities using Mana, a resource that is acquired both passively and through select abilities. Their most powerful spells are locked behind a higher Mana cost, but what those spells lose in early Round availability they make up for in sheer utility and damage. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/41b583a8b667a8273a8cd6d07206a39e8c4c8ef4.jpg
Case in point, pull them in and deal ALL OF THE DAMAGE. 

After finishing all the tutorial encounters, you’ll start the game with three Skill Cards:


 Thunderclap: Move, deal single-target damage, then Push an enemy away. 
 Stargate: Teleport to a desired location, then Swap a character to another location. If there’s someone already there, they’ll swap places!
 Gravity Nexus: Move, pull in all enemies within 3 hexes, then deal area-of-effect damage around the Arcanist. Then teleport to safety! 


You'll also gain an extra Skill Card that will always be available in your deck: Mana Spring. This ability allows you to regain a large amount of Mana based on how many characters are adjacent to you at the time of its use -- including enemies!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/d124cbb0a4d860c275a9ea19663962c5a504259f.jpg
Use your allies (and enemies) positions for your benefit. For mana. Manafit. 

A true scholar of the arcane arts, the Arcanist usually has a spell for every situation. And, as you level up, you'll unlock a variety of complex and interesting abilities like:

 Aetherize: An ability with a high Mana cost, but powerful single-target damage.
 Mirror Shatter: Oops too many decoys? Sacrifice them for even more damage. 
 Chaos Beam: Rewrite reality itself (within a line attack, at least).


Even more spells await you in-game, so if you’re interested in some hijinks, make sure to slot the Arcanist in your party! 

Fate Decks

Fate Cards are a core part of gameplay in Sunderfolk.

We'll be digging into this mechanic more in the future -- but, for now, just know that when a character performs an ability that includes an attack, they will draw a Fate Card from their Fate Deck. Based on the Fate Card that's drawn, that attack will then be augmented in some way.

Every character starts with a basic collection of Positive, Neutral, and Negative Fate cards that will impact the final damage output of their attacks. As you progress through the campaign, you’ll gain more and more Fate Cards, including ones that allow you to customize your character's build in fun and exciting ways.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/c69756436dc72f74161bec2d897cad4fdae27edd.png
Early level Fate Cards keep it simple, but as the game (and your knowledge) grows, so does the build customization! Neat!

For the Arcanist, some of these build options might focus on survivability, extra damage, debuffing enemies, or utilizing your unique spells – like spawning extra Decoys, for example. (Normally, you can only spawn Decoys by using a specific ability card. With this Fate Card, however, EVERY ability now has that chance, changing up your entire strategy.)

The Arcanist is truly a jack-of-all-trades when it comes to customizing their playstyle. 

 Want more damage for those sweet high-mana cost abilities? Give yourself Fate Cards that add Strength buffs for future setups. 
 Want to outdo the support characters with debuffs? Stack your deck with Fate Cards to Debuff ALL THE THINGS and set up for the ultimate KO. 
 Don’t want to use your precious turn to use Mana Spring for more Mana? Add more Fate Cards that refund or add Mana to your deck with a lucky draw. 


With some careful planning, you can make even the Negative Fate Cards work for your strategies. 

Ultimate Power

In Sunderfolk, characters unlock their Ultimate ability at Level 6 (once they've theoretically learned enough responsibility to manage it). These abilities are powerful and can be game-changing, depending on how you play. However, there's a catch! Each Ultimate has a cooldown, and only one Ultimate can be used per Round. This means communication is key -- you'll need to strategize with your fellow members to determine which character should use their Ultimate...and when!

In the case of the Arcanist, their Ultimate is Starfall. This area-of-effect spell packs a mean one-two punch, applying a Confusion debuff to every target it hits as well as stunning whatever enemy is at the center of its radius. (Note: Not only does Confusion cause affected creatures to potentially hit their friends, but it also makes you look REALLY cool when casting it.)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/815b5cde6b47b5464c3a26d649a35a03af49fc44.jpg
If you can’t get stars from the heavens, store-bought is fine. 

Speaking of stars… 

Up next in our “Meet the Hero” series is…the beat-dropping Bard!

- The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Meet the Heroes of Sunderfolk
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/657d82aaf689068d091cee90caa9cd21606c89cc.png

Meet Your Heroes

Safekeepers. Guardians. Heroes. 

The playable characters of Sunderfolk have many titles, but they all share the same mission—to protect the townsfolk of Arden. There are six different characters to choose from, and you’ll have the opportunity to play as one (in co-op) or up to four (if playing solo) during your adventures across the Sunderlands. 


 The Arcanist - Master the intricacies of the arcane!
 The Bard - Inspire and deceive with MUSIC!
 The Berserker - Channel your Rage and demolish foes!
 The Pyromancer - Engulf everything in red-hot flames!
 The Ranger - Hunt your opponent from a distance!
 The Rogue - Devastate prey with devious attacks!


Not only do they have their own unique relationships with residents in Arden, but you can create their own backstory that fits within your view of how they’ll interact with the world at large. 

In combat, each character has a unique playstyle that fills a vital role within a party. Don’t be deterred though! You’ll be able to proceed through the game with any combination—and, with the right strategy, you’ll always come out on top. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/5448a77dcbc105788efb81eae06b36a080be20aa.jpg
